{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.113","title":"draft-atwood-jmap-vtc: say a mesh call cannot negotiate, not only that it is not private","design":"HELD, not written. Mark 2026-11-25: "we have been flooding upstream,
just bead it instead for now." Split out of bead mimid-1wgh.114.15,
which is closed, so the wg half is not lost in it.

WHAT THE DRAFT SAYS NOW. draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 (~/PROJECT/
jmap-chat-spec/draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00.md, the paragraph on
VTCCallSignal):

  "A signal reaches every member of the call's MIMI room, because that
  is the granularity at which the room's MLS group encrypts. In a call
  whose media is peer-to-peer between two participants, or one whose
  media passes through a selective forwarding unit that is itself a
  participant, that is what is wanted. In a mesh call among three or
  more, the session description a participant intends for one peer is
  readable by all of them, so such a call gets no privacy between its
  own participants from this mechanism and MUST NOT be presented as
  though it did."

WHAT IT SHOULD ALSO SAY. A mesh call among three or more is not merely
unprivate, it is NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE. Nothing in a signal says which peer
it is for, and a mesh needs one offer per peer because each
PeerConnection has its own DTLS parameters and ICE ufrag, so N-1 offers
from one participant are indistinguishable to the receivers. A reader
who only minds the privacy warning could conclude a mesh is permissible
with consent. It is not implementable at all.

Two readings, and the draft should pick one:

1. Say so in that paragraph. One or two sentences, no wire change, and
   the capability field already lets a server state its ceiling
   (mimid now advertises maxParticipantsPerCall 2, bead
   mimid-1wgh.114.15).
2. Give VTCCall/signal an optional target participant id, which makes a
   mesh constructible. Addressing a signal does not require hiding it
   from the room; it only has to say whom it is for. Bigger, and it
   invites the question of why the room-wide broadcast remains.

WRITING IT NEEDS APPROVAL SEPARATELY from the flooding question: the
file is in ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec, and AGENTS.md requires Mark's OK
before any write there, each write its own approval.
